cards.caption: JPMorgan Chase says a cyberattack hit third-party service providers, and reports say Visa and Mastercard customer data was leaked by hackers. The story is drawing more than 5,000 US searches.
Florida is set to carry out its 20th execution, a record for the state, on the same day as a lethal injection in Texas. The AP reports both executions are proceeding on the same day.
Toyota is recalling more than 300,000 vehicles because of airbag degradation. Owners should check whether their model is included.
Trump says he is in no hurry to decide on new strikes against Iran, while reports say Israel is pushing for renewed action. The decision remains open for now.
The White Sox are reportedly trading Davis Martin and Luis Castillo to the Rockies, and the move is drawing strong US search interest. Details of the deal were not included in the headlines.
Boston's beloved Citgo sign is back after a rebuild, now 30 feet higher than before. The landmark returns to the skyline it has long defined.
Palestinians are fleeing as Israeli tanks cross the yellow line in Gaza, and NBC News reports the ceasefire is being tested. The headlines give no further details on casualties or what happens next.
The Los Angeles Times reports the cause of Patrick Stewart's death has been revealed. Fans are searching for the details.

Russian drones killed one person and damaged two European embassies and a cathedral during an hours-long raid on Kyiv, according to The Kyiv Independent. The strikes come as ceasefire diplomacy continues without a breakthrough.
California regulators approved an interim rate hike for PG&E customers for 2027, worth $456 million. Questions remain about $2 billion in proposed spending cuts.

A Senate plan to change Social Security would add $190 trillion to the national debt, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget. The estimate comes from a budget group, not an official scoring.

Intense flooding is hitting Florida as a developing tropical storm threatens to disrupt East Coast travel ahead of Thanksgiving. Forecasters say wind and rain could streak north this weekend into next week.
Poland's military is investigating two possible airspace violations during a Russian attack on Ukraine. Poland says flying objects entered its airspace.
Wall Street's fear gauge has hit its highest level in seven months, with worries about AI adding to the jitters. Traders are watching closely to see whether the nerves spread further.
A train heist reportedly netted $22.5M in goods, including Nike sneakers and Milwaukee tools, which one report calls staggering. The case shows how valuable cargo can be a target on the rails.

Truth Nigeria reports that airstrikes killed 21 ISWAP fighters and questions whether the militant network can survive. The figure comes from that outlet's reporting and has not been independently confirmed.

Billie Eilish has been announced as the first female headliner for BST Hyde Park's 2027 lineup, a date fans are already searching for. The Hyde Park show marks her first time headlining the London festival.

Russia struck three bridges in Kyiv in a massive aerial assault that the Kyiv Independent says left at least 9 dead. Putin has said Russia will not negotiate a limited ceasefire after the bridge strike.
Meta shares are down 21% as investors question whether the company is spending too much on AI. The slide may not be over yet.
New York Mayor Mamdani has proposed a five-year extension to the plan to shutter Rikers Island. The proposal would push back the timeline for closing the notorious jail.
Trump says he has pardoned deceased MLB slugger Pete Rose, a claim that comes from the president himself. The announcement has been reported by CBS News.
Reports say Iran is preparing an oil convoy to test the US blockade, and crude prices are heading for a third weekly loss. Fuel costs could be the next thing ordinary drivers feel.
Wayne Darling, a championship-winning NASCAR team owner and modified racing figure, has died, and the Seekonk racing community is remembering him. His death has hit the racing world hard.

A government watchdog report says ICE spent about $13 million a month on detention beds that went unused. The findings raise fresh questions about how taxpayer money is spent on immigration detention.
The UN has warned that strikes affecting Yemen's Hudaydah port could threaten a vital aid lifeline. The port sits at the centre of the warning.
The developer says Grand Theft Auto VI sales hit $3.8bn on its first day, which it calls a new record for entertainment. The launch is one of the biggest debuts the games industry has seen.
Denmark has expelled a Russian diplomat over an alleged plot to kill a Ukrainian rapper, according to Al Jazeera. The case adds a new diplomatic dispute to Russia's war on Ukraine.

Quentin Tarantino is drawing over 1000 US searches this hour as a review of David Fincher's Cliff Booth film makes the rounds. The film is set in Tarantino's world, and the reviewer says Fincher had to find himself in it first.
Congress is struggling to avert a US government shutdown as the Iran war divides lawmakers. Reuters is reporting the standoff as the deadline approaches.
The Nasdaq 100 just had its worst week since 2020 as an AI-driven selloff pushed the S&P 500 into correction territory. Trending searches show Americans are worried about where the market goes next.

Multiple reports say the United States and Israel are considering a new assault on Iran, with one former Navy chief suggesting a joint strike could come within weeks. Officials have not confirmed any timing.
The Hunger Games prequel Sunrise On The Reaping has opened its global weekend with a $76M running total, according to Deadline. The figure is still building as the weekend runs on.
Washington State has fined a company $9 million over a fatal tank implosion, according to The New York Times. The penalty puts a price on a deadly industrial failure.
Ukraine's General Staff has confirmed a strike on a key Druzhba oil pipeline station in Russia's Tatarstan region. Attacks on energy infrastructure can affect fuel prices far from the front line.
Donyell Malen scored four times for AS Roma in a standout performance that has fans searching for the match. It was a huge night for the club.
